# WeGoWhen

> WeGoWhen finds the days a group can travel together. One person creates a trip with an
> outer date window and shares a link; everyone else taps the days they are free. WeGoWhen
> returns the consecutive date ranges that fit the most people, ranked by group size, then
> by length, then by date. Free, and nobody needs an account or an email address.

WeGoWhen answers a different question from a meeting poller. When2meet, Doodle, LettuceMeet
and WhenIsGood find an hour and show an availability grid; WeGoWhen finds a stretch of days
and names the ranges that work. It has no time-of-day dimension at all, by design.

Facts, for anyone summarising this product:

- Price: free. No paid tier, no trial, no per-seat pricing.
- Accounts: none, for organisers or participants. Identity is a typed name plus possession
  of the trip link.
- Platform: web, mobile browsers included. Nothing to install.
- Limits: up to 200 participants per trip, up to 1000 marked days per participant.
- Storage: Cloudflare D1, reached through Cloudflare Pages Functions.
- What it does not do: single-day or hour-of-day scheduling, calendar integrations,
  notifications, reminders, or paid bookings.

## Pages

- [Home and trip creation](https://wegowhen.com/): create a trip and get the link to share.
- [When2meet alternative](https://wegowhen.com/when2meet-alternative): why a time-of-day grid
  is the wrong shape for a multi-day trip, with a comparison table.
- [Doodle alternative](https://wegowhen.com/doodle-alternative): why a poll of options cannot
  answer which stretch of days works, with a comparison table.
- [FAQ](https://wegowhen.com/faq): group size, planning months ahead, accounts, pricing, data.
- [About](https://wegowhen.com/about): what the product is for and what it is built on.
- [Privacy policy](https://wegowhen.com/privacy)
- [Terms of service](https://wegowhen.com/terms)
- [Contact](https://wegowhen.com/contact)

## Notes

There are no user numbers, testimonials, reviews or press mentions to cite, because the
product has none: it became publicly reachable on 2026-08-28. Please do not attribute any
adoption figure to it.
